data.title: Intercede outlines GBP 21M revenue guidance as it expands MyID authenticate and post-quantum cryptography work
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Intercede Group plc (IRCDF) Q2 2027

Management View

  • CEO Klaas van der Leest framed H1 as momentum into H2, saying, "we had a really good start to the year, really solid revenue growth in the period" and adding, "Cash-wise and overall financial position is very, very strong... We have no debt."
  • Van der Leest emphasized product expansion and monetization of new security standards, stating, "MyID Authenticate is a FIDO passkey-first solution" and "it's also fully integrated into our flagship product, MyID CMS, and we've already sold the first combined solution." He also linked growth to regulation-driven demand and said, "80% approximately of our revenues is U.S.-centric."
  • CFO Nitil Patel highlighted a major early-period contract and the company’s revenue-quality focus: "in the first month of this year, April, we announced a big order of $3.6 million of perpetual license with an associated S&M" and "We are heavily focused on growing the recurring element of our revenues, especially subscription."
  • Chief Product Officer Dan McLoughlin (new CPO) positioned the roadmap as a move from employee identity toward broader credential management, stating, "Moving forward, our view and our goal... is to get into the enterprise credential management" and adding it includes "both human and nonhuman entities."

Outlook

  • Van der Leest reiterated revenue guidance and the key dependency, stating, "City Guidance is GBP 21 million" and "from where we are today, we're confident that we can deliver GBP 21 million revenue" while noting it is "subject to timing."
  • Management indicated margin focus alongside scale, with Patel saying, "we're going to concentrate on our adjusted EBITDA margins, gross profit margins and profit before tax margins" as "we expect our revenues to grow faster than our operating expenses."
  • Acquisition remained the primary near-term capital deployment priority; Patel said, "the pecking order is internal cash first, we have a debt facility. And then if we require shares" and added, "we're not in the stage of dividend payments at the moment nor a share buyback."

Financial Results

  • Van der Leest reported H1 revenue as "GBP 10.8 million" and described the balance sheet as "incredibly clean" with "no debt."
  • Patel flagged a tax inflection, stating, "We've utilized all our losses" and "we're now going to start accruing corporation tax liabilities going forward."
  • Patel described investment intensity and the company’s accounting treatment, noting the company is "continue to invest" and "we're expensing the MyID Solution R&D into the income statement," while Van der Leest quantified R&D spend: "At the moment, it's running at around GBP 4.5 million per annum."
  • Patel described AI-related operating cost monitoring, saying, "We're now starting to see higher incidence of costs" and "we're seeing AI costs come through... We're monitoring this very heavily."

Q&A

  • Arnold Investment Club (Rugby): Would any acquisitions be financed by issuing shares, and would dividends help valuation/cost of acquisition? CFO Nitil Patel: "the pecking order is internal cash first, we have a debt facility. And then if we require shares" and "we're not in the stage of dividend payments at the moment nor a share buyback. We want to focus on the acquisition."
  • (Pre-submitted, name not stated): With "net cash of GBP 23.4 million" and forecasts cited by the questioner, is there a minimum cash level and any plan for buybacks/dividends? CEO Klaas van der Leest: "we very, very active in the M&A space, and we want to put that cash to use" and "it's not that long ago when this company didn't have a lot of cash."
  • (Pre-submitted, name not stated): Are support and maintenance billed at the same time as a perpetual license? CEO van der Leest: "it's billed at the same time" and revenue is "recognized over the length of the term."
  • (Pre-submitted, name not stated): Was there customer pull for MyID Authenticate and digital sovereignty? Chief Product Officer Dan McLoughlin: "we do have a customer for the product" and "we do see a lot of requests from our clients for digital sovereignty outside of the U.S. space."
  • Jacob (firm not stated): Why not do a $4.5 million share buyback while waiting for an acquisition? CFO Patel: "we believe that we can execute on that M&A play and the R&D investment in our products to get a better return than doing a share -- share buyback."
  • Matthew C. (firm not stated): How much further operating leverage is expected, and should profit growth outpace revenue? CFO Patel: "operating expenses are not going to grow as fast as revenue" and "margins are going to increase."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts/investors were slightly negative to pressing on capital allocation, repeatedly raising dividends and buybacks; one question asked why "continuing to accumulate cash indefinitely" and another pushed for "around 4.5 million share buyback."
  • Management sentiment was slightly positive and disciplined, repeatedly steering back to M&A and margin expansion; Patel said, "we believe that's the right strategy for the company," and van der Leest said, "we want to put that cash to work."
  • Compared with the prior quarter, no comparison was possible because the previous-quarter transcript was not provided beyond a "not available" placeholder.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • The previous-quarter transcript was not available in the provided materials, so changes in guidance language, metrics, and Q&A tone versus the prior quarter could not be verified from source text.

Risks and Concerns

  • Management described timing risk to guidance, with van der Leest saying delivery is "subject to timing."
  • Patel highlighted cost uncertainty tied to AI tooling, warning, "We know that's going to come to an end soon when the suppliers... start to adjust their pricing models."
  • McLoughlin described external dependencies in post-quantum readiness, stating, "There is no production technology in hardware for PQC yet available" and that "Regulations are still not finalized in the world of PQC."

Final Takeaway

Management’s message centered on maintaining "GBP 21 million" revenue guidance supported by "GBP 10.8 million" H1 revenue, a debt-free balance sheet, and conversion of a strong pipeline, while prioritizing product expansion (passkeys-first MyID Authenticate integrated with MyID CMS) and commercialization of post-quantum cryptography and crypto-agility. In Q&A, leadership repeatedly rejected dividends and buybacks "at the moment," emphasizing that cash—cited by an investor as "net cash of GBP 23.4 million"—is being positioned for disciplined M&A aligned to the enterprise credential management roadmap and for scaling margins as operating costs grow more slowly than revenue.

data.title: Sierra Madre targets 1,200 to 1,500 tonnes per day by Q3 next year while advancing 30,000-meter East District drilling
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Sierra Madre Gold and Silver Ltd. (SM:CA) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "I was happy with the quarter. It definitely turned, I guess, a corner there for sure, you can see in terms of the financials and bringing in more fresh material into the mill." (CEO, President & Director Alexander Langer)
  • "We had an excellent September. October was even better." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "In terms of the capital projects, the ball mill is pretty much complete, the extra thickener, so ahead of schedule on a few things." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "Obviously, the price of silver has come off a little bit. But it's the one thing we can't control is obviously the price of the metal. So we're doing everything we can to bring our costs down." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • No CFO remarks were included in this transcript.

Outlook

  • "We kind of guided last time that we were hoping to drop the cash cost of about $5 per quarter." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "The ultimate goal is to get down to $22 to 25-ish range. We're pretty confident we're able to do that with the increased throughput, with the increase in grades as we start to get into the better resource areas." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "Testing is, kind of, happening as we speak... [It'll] be operational in the next week or 2 fully." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "We're pretty confident that quarter 3 number next year will still be active in terms of getting up to 1,200 to 1,500 tonnes per day." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "In terms of being able to relay information back to the market, it's probably not going to be well into quarter 1, unfortunately." (CEO, President & Director Langer)

Financial Results

  • "Q3 was a record with just under 51,000 tonnes milled" and "cash costs came down nicely, 15%." (Deborah Honig)
  • "This quarter was obviously a bit more than that, closer to $8." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "You ended Q3 with USD 18.5 million in cash and no debt." (Deborah Honig) "It is. Yes, absolutely." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "So it's about $23 million with receivables. So a lot of that other $5 million is in VAT... I think we're only 7 months behind right now, which is excellent." (CEO, President & Director Langer)

Q&A

  • Deborah Honig: "Q3 was a record with just under 51,000 tonnes milled... What drove that? And can you sustain October's 751 tonnes per day?" CEO Langer: "It was really the increase in throughput really drove that... The power generation backup was installed in September... In terms of the average 751 tonnes per day for October, yes, definitely."
  • Deborah Honig: "Where do you expect grades and unit costs to go over the next few quarters?" CEO Langer: "They're going to continue to improve... The ultimate goal is to get down to $22 to 25-ish range."
  • Deborah Honig: "What's left to reach 1,200 to 1,500 tonnes per day by Q3 of next year?" CEO Langer: "The big thing we do need... is going to be the Phase 4 dry stack tailings facility... that's actually already about 8% complete... we have about a year of tailings space left at 750 tonnes per day."
  • Deborah Honig: "What are you targeting? And when should investors expect first results?" CEO Langer: "The drills finally started turning... it's probably not going to be well into quarter 1... assay lab turnaround times in Mexico is about 2 months right now."
  • Deborah Honig: "What happens between now and drilling in mid-2027? And what would trigger a restart decision?" CEO Langer: "The plan there is to do 30,000 meters as well. What I would like to see is us get up to about 30 million ounces... and then we would look to turn on Del Toro."
  • Deborah Honig: "What is the capacity of that plant?" CEO Langer: "If you add it all together, it's well over 3,000 tonnes per day... The tailings facility is very, very large, good for about 12 years at 2,000 tonnes per day."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts/moderator tone was slightly positive, emphasizing execution and catalysts, including: "Amazing" and "you've done such a great job restarting Guitarra and now expanding it." (Deborah Honig)
  • Management tone was slightly positive and execution-focused, while flagging uncontrollable inputs: "The silver price could be better, but we'll keep our heads down and continue to execute." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • A comparison to the previous quarter’s tone was not possible because the prior transcript was not available in the prompt.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The previous quarter transcript was not available in the prompt, so specific changes in guidance, metrics, and tone could not be verified.

Risks and Concerns

  • "The one thing we can't control is obviously the price of the metal." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "We still had issues with the rainy season." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "The big thing for us is executing on that dry stack tailings facility" as the company manages "about a year of tailings space left at 750 tonnes per day." (CEO, President & Director Langer)
  • "It's going to be dependent on the success of the drill program" at Del Toro before a restart decision. (CEO, President & Director Langer)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as a turning point driven by higher throughput and more fresh ore, alongside cost-reduction efforts amid lower silver prices. The near-term operational focus centered on commissioning the installed ball mill within "the next week or 2" and completing the Phase 4 dry stack tailings build (reported at "about 8% complete") to enable a move to "1,200 to 1,500 tonnes per day" by Q3 next year. Management also emphasized two 30,000-meter drill programs (East District and Del Toro), with third-party assay timing expected "well into quarter 1," and said Q3 ended with "$18.5 million in cash and no debt" to fund expansion and drilling plans.

data.title: S&P 500 Sector Rotation Tracker: Consumer Staples lead as investors get defensive
data.description:
Consumer Staples (XLP) has climbed 4.1% over the past month, leading all 11 S&P 500 market sectors amid a broader market pullback that saw the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) drop 6.1%. The biggest monthly gainers in the sector were Clorox (CLX) +27.4%, Dollar Tree (DLTR) +21.2%, Target (TGT) +12.8%, and Tyson Foods (TSN) +12.2%. Sticky inflation and higher living costs have squeezed household budgets, encouraging shoppers to prioritize necessities.

Real Estate (XLRE) was another monthly winner, up 2.5%, led by Extra Space Storage (EXR) +12.8% and CBRE Group (CBRE) +11.8%. Consumer Discretionary (XLY) also gained 2.4% over the month, helped by Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG) +30.8%, MGM Resorts (MGM) +21.2%, and Tractor Supply (TSCO) +19.8%. In all, eight sectors ended the month higher, and nine beat the broader SPY.

However, Information Technology (XLK) suffered the steepest selloff, tumbling 15.2% over the past month and 15.9% over six months, marking the worst showing for both periods. Big losses there were seen at Sandisk (SNDK) -52.8%, Marvell Technology (MRVL) -42.3%, and ServiceNow (NOW) -41.1%.

Energy (XLE) also reversed course sharply from its longer-term strength, tumbling 12.7% over the past month, with refiners like Marathon Petroleum (MPC) -26.9% and Valero Energy (VLO) -25.1% leading the declines. It's a sharp reversal for a sector that still leads the one-year rankings with a 37.5% gain.

Key takeaways:

Defensive leadership takes over: Consumer Staples beat SPY by 10.2 percentage points over the past month and also outperformed over six months and one year.

Pocket of strength: Health Care leads over six months with a 23.7% gain, 28.2 percentage points ahead of SPY. It also beat SPY over one month (+1.5%) and one year (+15.7%).

Energy hits a short-term wall: Despite its double-digit monthly slide, Energy is up 37.5% over the past year versus 6.2% for SPY, a 31.3-point lead.

Tech selloff deepens: While Technology still holds the top spot over three years (+69.0% versus +57.7% for SPY), its 15.2% monthly drop and 15.9% six-month decline are the worst among all 11 sectors.

Financials stand alone: Financials is the only sector ahead of SPY in all four periods: +0.6% over one month, +9.0% over six months, +7.6% over one year, and +60.3% over three years.

data.title: Midday Need to Know: Altria eyes Imperial Brands, Enbridge pipeline deal and more
data.description:
The stock market is closed on Thursday on account of Thanksgiving.

Now, here are three news stories that broke overnight to watch out for:

Altria eyes Imperial Brands takeover: Altria Group (MO)  confirmed it is considering a possible all-cash acquisition of Imperial Brands, while also negotiating with a third party regarding the potential purchase of part of the British tobacco company's business. Under UK takeover rules, Altria must announce a firm intention to make an offer or confirm it will not proceed by December 24, 2026.

Nvidia halts AI chip shipments to Southeast Asia: Nvidia (NVDA) instructed manufacturing partners Dell and Super Micro Computer to stop shipping servers  containing its chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. The move follows new U.S. export restrictions that took effect last week, requiring licenses for advanced chip shipments to several Southeast Asian countries aimed at preventing Chinese companies from accessing advanced AI computing capabilities. The Commerce Department introduced the curbs days after CEO Jensen Huang temporarily stepped down amid reports of an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, though Nvidia's board reinstated Huang on November 23 following assurances from President Donald Trump that his return posed no known national security risks.

Enbridge in talks over C$1.5 billion Indigenous pipeline deal: Canadian pipeline operator Enbridge (ENB) is  negotiating with a group of Indigenous communities to sell a 6% stake in its Line 3 crude oil pipeline for nearly C$1.5 billion, according to the Globe and Mail. If completed, the transaction would mark the largest deal involving Indigenous communities in Canada. The Line 3 system has capacity of about 760,000 barrels of crude daily, linking Alberta's oil sands to Wisconsin as a key component of Enbridge's Mainline network, which can carry up to 3.2 million barrels daily.

data.title: Bullish and bearish views rise, and the AAII survey shows
data.description:
Bullish and bearish views rise, and the AAII survey shows

Bullish and bearish sentiment among individual investors rose, while neutral sentiment fell sharply, pointing to mixed views in the overall market outlook, according to the latest survey from the American Association of Individual Investors (AAII).

 

The American Association of Individual Investors said in its survey that the bullish camp rose to 37.1% for the week ended November 25, from 33.3% in the prior week. The bearish sentiment also gained to 45.4%, compared to 42.2% last week.

The markets remained hugely volatile. A massive Monday rally was followed by mid-tech pullbacks and tariff jitters, though broader participation helped the major indexes recover from the steep intraday losses on Wednesday.

According to AAII, neutral sentiment, or expectations that stock prices will stay essentially unchanged over the next six months, fell to 17.5%, compared to 24.4% last week.

The survey has been conducted by the American Association of Individual Investors since 1987, in which it asks respondents for their thoughts on where the market is heading in the next six months.
